feed.title: Outbreak Ledger
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced outbreak trackers. Every claim linked.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: No plague found in contacts tested so far
entry.summary: Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.
entry.content:
Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.

Sources: NBC News, U.S. News

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Russia tells WHO no plague found in contacts; WHO rates the risk
entry.summary: Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.
entry.content:
Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.

Sources: UN News, NBC News, PBS NewsHour

entry.title: Measles · US: Pennsylvania passes 1,000 cases; New York declares a disaster emergency
entry.summary: Pennsylvania reaches 1,004 cases in 39 counties, the first US state past 1,000 in a year since 1991. New York's governor declares a state disaster emergency through 4 November and lets pharmacists, paramedics and midwives vaccinate.
entry.content:
Pennsylvania reaches 1,004 cases in 39 counties, the first US state past 1,000 in a year since 1991. New York's governor declares a state disaster emergency through 4 November and lets pharmacists, paramedics and midwives vaccinate.

Sources: Pennsylvania Dept. of Health, Philadelphia Inquirer, New York Governor's office, NBC News

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya's first imported case dies in Nairobi
entry.summary: A Kenyan citizen living in DR Congo travelled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. He tested positive and died on 5 October. Contacts are being followed.
entry.content:
A Kenyan citizen living in DR Congo travelled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. He tested positive and died on 5 October. Contacts are being followed.

Sources: WHO Africa, Citizen Digital

entry.content:

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries
entry.summary: WHO's August update, now published in its Weekly Epidemiological Record, covers 1 January to 30 August: 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier. August's 41,915 new cases were 25% fewer than July's. Nigeria (69,263) and DR Congo (44,773) report the most cases in Africa.
entry.content:
WHO's August update, now published in its Weekly Epidemiological Record, covers 1 January to 30 August: 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier. August's 41,915 new cases were 25% fewer than July's. Nigeria (69,263) and DR Congo (44,773) report the most cases in Africa.

Sources: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record (2 Oct)

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Death confirmed; Shelekhov hospital quarantined
entry.summary: She dies overnight on 1–2 October. Governor Igor Kobzev cites a suspected "particularly dangerous infection". Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova flies in for an emergency commission. 197 contacts are identified and 189 hospitalised for observation. Kobzev says none have symptoms and all tests are negative.
entry.content:
She dies overnight on 1–2 October. Governor Igor Kobzev cites a suspected "particularly dangerous infection". Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova flies in for an emergency commission. 197 contacts are identified and 189 hospitalised for observation. Kobzev says none have symptoms and all tests are negative.

Sources: The Moscow Times, NBC News

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: 2025 had the most cholera deaths since 1999
entry.summary: 47 countries reported 451,499 cases and 7,870 deaths to WHO in 2025. Deaths rose 30% although fewer cases were reported, and seven countries accounted for about 90% of cases and deaths. WHO says the true burden is substantially higher.
entry.content:
47 countries reported 451,499 cases and 7,870 deaths to WHO in 2025. Deaths rose 30% although fewer cases were reported, and seven countries accounted for about 90% of cases and deaths. WHO says the true burden is substantially higher.

Sources: WHO, Down To Earth, The Guardian Nigeria

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: CDC says sustained clade Ib spread in the US is likely
entry.summary: CDC counts more than 60 confirmed clade I cases in at least 20 states since November 2024. Since August, more cases have had no travel link, and presumed local spread in more than 10 jurisdictions points to a likely transition to sustained transmission. CDC rates the risk to most people as low.
entry.content:
CDC counts more than 60 confirmed clade I cases in at least 20 states since November 2024. Since August, more cases have had no travel link, and presumed local spread in more than 10 jurisdictions points to a likely transition to sustained transmission. CDC rates the risk to most people as low.

Sources: CDC: clade I outbreaks, CDC: current situation

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: South Africa reports 22 cases, likely clade Ib
entry.summary: The health department counts 22 laboratory-confirmed cases as of 22 September: 18 in the Western Cape, 3 in Gauteng and 1 in KwaZulu-Natal. Thirteen of the Western Cape cases were confirmed since mid-August, and preliminary analysis points to clade Ib in both clusters.
entry.content:
The health department counts 22 laboratory-confirmed cases as of 22 September: 18 in the Western Cape, 3 in Gauteng and 1 in KwaZulu-Natal. Thirteen of the Western Cape cases were confirmed since mid-August, and preliminary analysis points to clade Ib in both clusters.

Sources: South African Government, TimesLIVE, EWN

entry.title: Dengue · Europe: Italy confirms its first local outbreaks of 2026

Sources: AgenSalute (ISS data), Italpress, Biomedical CuE, Sanità Informazione
